defects.quote: Teams that adopt Kubernetes spend 60% of their engineering time on infrastructure.
Google needs Kubernetes and you are not Google, so you do not need it.
defects.known_rebuttal: Whether an orchestrator is worth it depends on operational requirements, not on company size. A small team running several services still needs rolling deploys, health checks, restarts, autoscaling and secret management, and the alternative is usually a home-grown set of scripts that nobody else knows. Managed services such as GKE, EKS and AKS remove most of the control-plane burden, and a standard API brings portability, a large ecosystem and engineers who already know it.
